facts.detail: The 2024 to 2025 plan is a companion to BDUK's multi-year 2023 to 2026 Corporate Plan.
It focuses on objectives for the year ending 31 March 2025.
The plan describes Project Gigabit as a £5 billion programme.
The programme targets homes and businesses that would not otherwise be connected by suppliers' commercial plans.
The plan links the programme to the target of nationwide gigabit-capable broadband by 2030.

guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK Delivery Performance, annual: April 2025 to March 2026

facts.detail: BDUK estimated 192,570 premises received subsidised gigabit-capable coverage in 2025/26.
Annual delivery increased by 42,280 premises, or 28%, compared with the previous financial year.
Voucher schemes contributed 16% of annual delivery, equal to 30,530 premises.
England accounted for 75% of annual delivery, equal to 145,110 premises.
Residential properties represented 90% of delivered premises, equal to 173,270.

facts.detail: BDUK publishes the page as monthly contract-level Project Gigabit progress data.
Contracted-premises figures cover only the initial contract scope.
Deferred-scope premises may not be reflected in the contracted-premises figures.
The contract data is not directly comparable with BDUK official-statistics delivery figures.
Supplier data resubmissions removed earlier records pending replacement, so comparisons require caution.

guard_streams.source: New Ofcom research reveals how to cut phone and internet bills

facts.detail: Ofcom published the bill-savings research announcement on 26 February 2026.
The announcement was last updated on 30 June 2026.
The research covers phone, broadband and pay-TV customer bills.
Ofcom highlights end-of-contract alerts, simpler contract summaries and easier switching reforms.
Ofcom describes its annual pricing and consumer-engagement report as a comprehensive market analysis.
